detailed_summary: The paper introduces a logical-qubit representation for orbital angular momentum (OAM) propagation through turbulent channels, treating OAM modes as qubits that evolve under noisy quantum channels. In this framework, atmospheric turbulence is modeled as leakage from the logical OAM subspace into turbulence-induced leakage components, providing a unified description of degradation for both single-photon and coherent-beam regimes. The authors show that this leakage depends systematically on turbulence strength and OAM order, revealing structured signatures of information redistribution beyond the logical subspace. They then develop a distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme that encodes high-dimensional OAM states into quantum representations and applies quantum convolutional operations to extract turbulence-robust features. Simulations and experimental measurements demonstrate that these features can be extracted robustly across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions. The work establishes a direct link between OAM-channel dynamics, structured leakage, and quantum learning, offering a physics-informed framework for characterizing turbulence-degraded high-dimensional optical states and extracting robust signatures of turbulence-induced information redistribution.

Unified description of turbulence-induced degradation for both single-photon and coherent-beam regimes within the same quantum channel formalism.
Demonstration that turbulence-induced leakage exhibits systematic dependence on turbulence strength and OAM order, revealing structured information redistribution.
Development of a distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme using quantum convolutional operations to extract turbulence-robust features from high-dimensional OAM states.
Validation through simulations and experimental measurements across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions.
methodology_analysis: The authors model OAM propagation as a quantum channel acting on a logical qubit subspace, where turbulence induces leakage into other OAM modes. This is formalized by treating the OAM mode space as a high-dimensional Hilbert space and projecting onto a logical subspace, with leakage characterized by the population outside this subspace. The approach unifies single-photon and coherent-beam regimes by considering the evolution of the density matrix or field quadratures under the same channel description. For feature extraction, they design a distributed quantum feature-extraction scheme that encodes OAM states into quantum representations and applies quantum convolutional operations—likely parameterized quantum circuits acting as convolutional filters—to learn turbulence-robust features. The methodology combines analytical modeling of the channel with numerical simulations and experimental validation, though specific details of the quantum convolutional architecture and training procedure are not fully elaborated in the provided text.
results_analysis: The paper reports that turbulence-induced leakage depends systematically on turbulence strength (e.g., refractive index structure constant Cn^2) and OAM order (ℓ), with higher OAM orders experiencing greater leakage. This structured dependence is observed in both simulations and experiments. The quantum feature-extraction scheme successfully extracts robust features across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions, as evidenced by improved classification or reconstruction performance compared to baseline methods. connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics and related fields, particularly quantum communication and quantum information processing with high-dimensional systems. It addresses a key challenge in free-space quantum communication—turbulence-induced decoherence—by applying quantum channel formalism and quantum machine learning. The logical-qubit representation and leakage analysis connect to broader studies of quantum error correction and decoherence in continuous-variable and discrete-variable systems. The use of quantum convolutional operations for feature extraction also ties into quantum machine learning and quantum-enhanced sensing, areas of active interest in quantum physics.
